info.title: Speedtest Watcher API
info.description:
Results, statistics, settings, backups and metrics of a Speedtest Watcher instance.

- **Authentication:** while sign-in is off, no token is needed. While it's on, create a token under **Settings → Security → API Token** and send it as `Authorization: Bearer swt_…`. Read operations also work without a token when people who aren't signed in have read-only access.
- **Errors** answer with `{ "message": "…" }` and a 4xx status. `401` means the request needs a valid token.
- **Units:** timestamps are UTC ISO 8601, speeds are Mbps, ping and jitter are milliseconds, and test durations are seconds. Failed and skipped results have `-1` readings.

The guide, with examples, is at https://github.com/remotesojourner/speedtest-watcher/blob/main/docs/api.md.

get.description:
Returns every setting the caller may see as a string, plus flags about sign-in. Read-only visitors don't get the settings marked full access only. Sign-in settings are managed on the Security tab and secrets are never returned.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

patch.description:
Saves one or more settings together: either every change is saved or none is. Keys are the setting names from `GET /api/config`, and values are strings. Send `none` to unset an optional value. Sign-in settings can only be changed on the Security tab.

Open browser tabs, the scheduler and integrations pick the changes up straight away.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

400.description: A key is unknown or managed on the Security tab, or a value isn't allowed. Nothing was saved.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
A 1200 by 600 PNG with the latest completed test's ping, download and upload, for chat apps and social sites that show a preview of a shared link.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
The latest readings in the Prometheus text format, each prefixed with `speedtest_watcher_`. Readings come from the latest completed test, so a failed or skipped test leaves no gaps. `last_test_timestamp_seconds` shows when any test last ran and `last_completed_test_timestamp_seconds` when one last completed.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
The best ping, download and upload of the last 10 completed tests, updated after every completed test.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Returns results newest first. To get the next page, pass the `id` of the last result you received as `afterId`. An `afterId` that doesn't exist gives an empty list.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many results to return. 0 or less gives 10.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only results started this way: `auto` by the schedule, `custom` by hand.

parameters.name: healthy
parameters.description: Only results that met (`true`) or missed (`false`) their targets.

400.description: A filter has a value that isn't allowed.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description: **Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

delete.description: **Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Summarises the tests in a period: counts, the lowest, average and highest readings, how steady they were, averages per hour of the day, and points for charts.

`from` and `to` each take a date (`2026-09-14`), which covers that whole day, or a date and time. A time without an offset is read in `tz`. A value that can't be read falls back to the default.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period. Defaults to seven days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: An IANA time zone, such as `Europe/London`, for day boundaries and the hourly averages. Defaults to UTC.

400.description: The time zone isn't one the server knows.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

post.description:
Downloads the matching results as a CSV or JSON file, oldest first. A JSON export can be imported again with `PUT /api/storage/tests/history`.

**Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

requestBody.description: Which results to export and in what format.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description: **Access:** read. Works for everyone while sign-in is off, and for read-only visitors, signed-in users and API tokens while it's on.

200.description: Whether a test is running and whether tests are paused.

401.description: Sign-in is on, people who aren't signed in have no access, and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

post.description:
Starts a manual test and answers straight away, while the test runs in the background. Poll `GET /api/speedtests/status` or the result list to see when it has finished.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

parameters.name: serverId
parameters.description: Test against this server instead of the configured choice. Only providers with server choice use it.

400.description: The server id isn't a number.

409.description: A test is already running, tests are paused, or no provider is chosen.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

post.description:
Stops scheduled and manual tests. A test that is already running finishes. The pause is kept in memory, so restarting the app resumes tests.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

requestBody.description: How long to pause. Send no body, or leave `resumeIn` out, to pause until tests are resumed.

400.description: The pause is longer than 720 hours.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

post.description: **Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

200.description: Tests are running on schedule again.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description: **Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

200.description: The database size and how many results are stored.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Downloads `speedtests.json`, oldest first. It can be imported again with `PUT /api/storage/tests/history`.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Downloads `speedtests.csv`, oldest first. Text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula is escaped.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

put.description:
Adds results from a JSON export. Ids in the file are ignored, and results whose timestamp is already stored are skipped, so importing the same file twice is safe.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

requestBody.description: The results, in the format of a JSON export.

200.description: How many results were imported and skipped.

400.description: The list is empty or isn't valid.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

delete.description:
Clears the history. Settings, integrations and recommendations stay. This can't be undone.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Returns the settings, integrations and recommendations in the format of the Storage tab's backup file. Sign-in settings are never included.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

put.description:
Saves the valid settings together, adds or replaces integrations by id, and restores the recommendations when all three values are positive. Anything that isn't valid, and any sign-in setting, is skipped and counted.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

requestBody.description: A backup from `GET /api/storage/config` or the Storage tab.

200.description: What was restored and how much was skipped.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

get.description:
Returns this instance's version and the latest release on GitHub. The release is checked at most every six hours, or every hour after a failed check.

**Access:** full. Needs sign-in to be off, a signed-in browser session, or an API token.

401.description: Sign-in is on and the request has no valid API token or signed-in session.

timestamp.description: When the test ran, or the middle of the slice, in UTC.

failed.description: Whether the test, or any test in the slice, failed.

error.description: Why the test failed, or how many tests in the slice failed.

duration.description: How long the test took, in seconds.

ChartPointResponse.description: One point on the charts: a single test, or the average of the tests in a slice of the period. Readings are `null` when no test in it completed.

authActive.description: Sign-in is switched on and enforced.

authDisabledByEnv.description: Sign-in is switched off by the `DISABLE_AUTH` environment variable.

oidcClientSecretSet.description: A client secret is saved for the identity provider. Left out for read-only visitors.

apiTokenSet.description: An API token exists. Left out for read-only visitors.

ping.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

download.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

upload.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

provider.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

interface.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

serverMode.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

serverListMode.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

internetCheckEnabled.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

chartRange.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

chartBeginAtZero.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

dateFormat.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

retentionDays.description: Visible to everyone who can read the settings.

authEnabled.description: Changed only on the Security tab. Left out for read-only visitors.

visitorAccess.description: Changed only on the Security tab. Left out for read-only visitors.

oidcAuthority.description: Changed only on the Security tab. Left out for read-only visitors.

oidcClientId.description: Changed only on the Security tab. Left out for read-only visitors.

oidcScopes.description: Changed only on the Security tab. Left out for read-only visitors.

ConfigResponse.description: The saved settings, one string property per setting, plus what the caller may see and do. Unset values are `none`. Read-only visitors don't get the settings marked full access only, and secrets are never returned.

ConsistencyResponse.description: How steady the readings of the completed tests were. All values are `0` when no test completed.

message.description: What went wrong, written for people.

ErrorResponse.description: Why a request failed. Every error the API answers carries this body.

format.description: `csv` or `json`. Anything else gives CSV. The JSON can be imported again.

healthy.description: Only results that met (`true`) or missed (`false`) their targets.

ids.description: Only these results. The other filters still apply.

ExportResultsRequest.description: Which results to export and in what format. Leave everything out to export every result as CSV.

hour.description: The hour of the day, 0 to 23, in the requested time zone.

count.description: How many completed tests ran in this hour.

download.description: Average download speed in Mbps, or `null` when no test ran in this hour.

upload.description: Average upload speed in Mbps, or `null` when no test ran in this hour.

ping.description: Average ping in milliseconds, or `null` when no test ran in this hour.

jitter.description: Average jitter in milliseconds, or `null` when no test in this hour reported it.

HourlyAverageResponse.description: Averages of the completed tests that ran in one hour of the day.

MessageResponse.description: Confirms that a request which changes something succeeded.

avg.description: The average, rounded to two decimals. Ping and time averages are rounded to whole numbers.

MetricSummaryResponse.description: The lowest, average and highest value of one reading.

resumeIn.description: Resume automatically after this many hours, at most 720 (30 days). Leave it out to pause until tests are resumed.

stdDev.description: The standard deviation of ping, in milliseconds.

jitter.description: The same standard deviation, kept for older dashboards.

download.description: The highest download speed, in Mbps.

upload.description: The highest upload speed, in Mbps.

RecommendationResponse.description: Suggested targets: the best ping, download and upload of the last 10 completed tests.

paused.description: Scheduled and manual tests are paused.

RunStatusResponse.description: Whether a speedtest is running and whether tests are paused.

recommendations.description: The recommended targets, or `null` before 10 tests have completed.

SettingsBackup.description: A settings backup: the settings, integrations and recommendations, in the same format as the file the Storage tab exports. Sign-in settings are never included.

SettingsBackupEntry.description: One saved setting in a backup.

id.description: The integration's id. An import replaces the integration with the same id.

displayName.description: The name shown on the Integrations tab.

name.description: The integration type, such as `webhook`, `discord` or `influxdb`.

data.description: The integration's settings, as a JSON object written out as a string.

lastActivity.description: When the integration last sent something, in UTC.

SettingsBackupIntegration.description: One configured integration in a backup.

id.description: The stored row's id. It is ignored on import.

download.description: The recommended download speed, in Mbps.

upload.description: The recommended upload speed, in Mbps.

SettingsBackupRecommendation.description: The recommended targets in a backup. They're restored only when all three values are positive.

integrations.description: Integrations that were added or replaced.

skipped.description: Entries that were left out because they weren't valid, such as unknown settings or integration types.

SettingsImportResponse.description: What a settings backup import restored.

consistency.description: 100 minus the standard deviation as a percentage of the average, never below 0. 100 means every test got the same speed.

created.description: When the test ran, in UTC.

status.description: Whether the test completed, failed, or was skipped before it ran.

type.description: What started the test: `auto` for the schedule, `custom` for a manual run.

ping.description: Latency in milliseconds, or `-1` when the test didn't complete.

jitter.description: Jitter in milliseconds, when the provider reports it.

download.description: Download speed in Mbps, or `-1` when the test didn't complete.

upload.description: Upload speed in Mbps, or `-1` when the test didn't complete.

time.description: How long the test took, in seconds.

healthy.description: Whether the result met the targets it was judged against. `null` when the test didn't complete or no targets were set.

thresholdPing.description: The highest acceptable ping, in milliseconds, when the test ran.

thresholdDownload.description: The lowest acceptable download speed, in Mbps, when the test ran.

thresholdUpload.description: The lowest acceptable upload speed, in Mbps, when the test ran.

error.description: Why the test failed or was skipped.

serverId.description: The id of the server the test ran against, or `0` when there was none.

serverName.description: The name of the server the test ran against.

serverHost.description: The host of the server the test ran against.

resultId.description: The provider's own id for the result, such as Ookla's result id.

packetLoss.description: Packet loss as a percentage, when the provider measures it. Only Ookla does.

downloadBytes.description: Bytes downloaded during the test, when the provider reports them.

uploadBytes.description: Bytes uploaded during the test, when the provider reports them.

publicIp.description: The public IP the test ran from, when the pre-test check looked it up. Only for full access; read-only visitors get `null`.

SpeedtestResponse.description: One stored speedtest result. Failed and skipped results have `-1` for ping, download and upload.

from.description: The start, as requested, or seven days ago.

to.description: The end, as requested, or today.

days.description: How many days the period spans, rounded up.

tests.description: How many tests ran in the period and how many of them failed.

ping.description: Ping of the completed tests, in milliseconds. `null` when none completed.

jitter.description: Jitter of the completed tests, in milliseconds. `null` when none reported jitter.

download.description: Download speed of the completed tests, in Mbps. `null` when none completed.

upload.description: Upload speed of the completed tests, in Mbps. `null` when none completed.

time.description: How long the completed tests took, in seconds. `null` when none completed.

consistency.description: How steady the completed tests' readings were.

packetLoss.description: Packet loss across the completed tests that measured it, as percentages. Only Ookla measures it.

dataUsedBytes.description: Bytes the tests in the period moved, download and upload together, as far as the providers reported them.

hourlyAverages.description: Averages of the completed tests for each hour of the day, 0 to 23, in the requested time zone.

points.description: Chart points, oldest first. Up to 300 tests give one point each. More are averaged into 300 equal slices of the period, and slices without tests are left out.

rawDataPoints.description: How many tests ran in the period, before any averaging.

downsampled.description: Whether the points were averaged down from more tests.

StatisticsResponse.description: Summary figures and chart points for a period.

size.description: The size of the SQLite database, in bytes.

total.description: Every test in the period, including failed and skipped ones.

TestCountsResponse.description: How many tests ran in a period.

skipped.description: Results that were left out because a result with the same timestamp is already stored.

created.description: When the test ran. A time without an offset is read as UTC. A result with the same timestamp as a stored one is skipped.

status.description: `completed`, `failed` or `skipped`. Anything else counts as `failed` when there's an error, and as `completed` otherwise.

time.description: How long the test took, in seconds.

healthy.description: Whether the result met its targets.

thresholdPing.description: The ping target, in milliseconds, when the test ran.

thresholdDownload.description: The download target, in Mbps, when the test ran.

thresholdUpload.description: The upload target, in Mbps, when the test ran.

error.description: Why the test failed or was skipped.

serverId.description: The id of the server the test ran against.

serverName.description: The name of the server the test ran against.

serverHost.description: The host of the server the test ran against.

resultId.description: The provider's own id for the result.

TestImportRow.description: One result to import, in the format of a JSON export. Ids in the file are ignored.

remote.description: The latest release on GitHub, or `0` when it couldn't be checked. It is checked at most every six hours.

VersionResponse.description: The running version and the latest release.

apiToken.description: An API token (`swt_…`) from **Settings → Security → API Token**. It's needed only while sign-in is on, and read operations don't need it when people who aren't signed in have read-only access.
